We pursued four approaches: (1) defining key parameters of the lamination window and optimizing the process to control the properties and performance of the EEA laminate; (2) scale-up of the process to demonstrate fabrication of >10 ft EEA laminate; (3) using slot-die coating to increase the throughput of EEA fabrication to target >5 m/min for the thick, anode layer; and (4) minimization of the anode thickness to reduce material cost. Results accumulated throughout the execution of the project will create the following benefits:  > 10 fold increase in manufacture speed of anode support layer (ASL)  > 30% reduction in manufacture cost  > tenfold reduction of material cost  no loss in performance versus cells made using conventional manufacturing Demonstrating the fabrication of > 10 ft of the EEA laminate, closes remaining technical gaps and paves the way forward for the commercialization readiness of this technology. The major project goals remaining to be met is:  confirmation of the fabricated cell using this process demonstrates no loss in performance versus cells made using conventional manufacturing. The cell processing and performance test role was the responsibility of project partner Redox, which became non-responsive during the project implementation. Due to management changes in the company, this goal had not been completed in the agreed upon timeline. ORNL initiated this portion of work and intends to collaborate with a new CRADA partner to finish the project. 1. PROJECT ACCOMPLISHMENTS 2.1 Q1: Green tapes of the three separate EEA layers, that had been tape cast by the project partner (Redox), were received by the ORNL team, and were documented and photographed. Their general characterization was used to provide a standard benchmark on the appearance, color and thickness of the anode support layer (ASL), anode functional layer (AFL) and gadolinium-doped cerium oxide (GDC) layer. Screening of the lamination window was initiated for the ASL-ASL target laminate and carried out at various conditions using the calender at the Department of Energy
